summary: Embedding precision truncation causing rerank order inversions for search results
description:
Issue summary: Customer Findly reports that after a recent model rollout and automatic embedding-quantization optimization, search rerank orders for a subset of queries have inverted (previously top-3 items fall to bottom and vice versa).

Impact: Affecting several product search flows for Findly's production workspace on Dedicated capacity in us-east-1. Visible to ~2% of queries (but high business impact since these queries are high-conversion).

Environment: Dedicated cluster (pool-id d-101), embeddings served by rwd-embed-quant8-v2 variant in prod:us-east. Reranker service uses cosine similarity over 1024-d vectors; downstream ranking uses softmax on scores.

Expected behavior: Embeddings computed after rollout should be backward-compatible in ordering for high-similarity pairs; rank stability metric should not regress beyond thresholds.

Actual behavior: For certain queries, result order is inverted despite only small L2 differences. The shift appears correlated with embeddings produced by the quantized variant (rwd-embed-quant8-v2), while the full-precision model (rwd-embed-large-v2) shows expected ordering.

Additional context: Findly attached sample query IDs and old vs new embedding vectors (hashed). Customer observed change immediately after we enabled an aggressive precision-trimming optimization on the Dedicated pool intended to reduce memory and bandwidth.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Findly prod workspace on d-101 (us-east) with model rwd-embed-quant8-v2.
2) Run the provided canonical query set (attached in comments).
3) Generate embeddings via /v1/embeddings and run rerank endpoint (POST /v1/rerank) using cosine similarity on returned vectors.
4) Compare top-5 orders against same queries generated with rwd-embed-large-v2 on a non-quantized pool.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: precision truncation from int8 quantization is amplifying small angular differences, changing cosine orderings for near-tie vectors.

Reproduced locally by forcing quantize(embedding) and comparing pairwise cosine deltas between fp32->int8->fp32 upcast paths; observed sign flips in ~0.9% of pairs where true cosine difference < 1e-3.

Observed that our on-the-fly upcast used nearest-neighbor dequantization without the original scale/bias metadata in some Dedicated deployments — leading to inconsistent reconstruction of float vectors.

Caching interplay: prefix/KV cache was returning pre-quantized vectors for some requests while other requests invoked fresh computation with a different scale; mismatch surfaced in cross-batch reranking.
No evidence of NaNs or 5xx; scores are valid floats but ordering changed due to subtle numeric artifacts.

2026-03-10 12:15 - Jonas Kim (SRE): Reproduced locally on staging by toggling quantization flags. Found pairwise sign flips for near-tie examples. Added logs to reranker to capture original model variant.

2026-03-11 08:40 - Nina Roberts (ML Infra): Confirmed that embeddings-service omitted scale metadata in cache entries for the quantized pipeline in certain Dedicated pool upgrades. Working on a patch to include full quantization params in cache payloads.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Support (Maya): Notified Findly we are investigating; provided temporary mitigation: pin workspace to rwd-embed-large-v2 and disabled auto-quant for their pool.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Jonas Kim (SRE): Deployed hotfix to include quantization metadata in cache and added validation to reject cache items lacking scale/bias. Rolling out to d-101 in canary (10%).
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer workspace pinned to rwd-embed-large-v2 and auto-quant disabled for their Dedicated pool. Hotfix deployed to embeddings-service to persist and transmit quantization scale/bias alongside int8 payloads. Validation added so cache entries without metadata are invalidated.

Planned permanent fix: Update quantization pipeline to use per-channel scales and deterministic rounding, add end-to-end unit tests for order-preservation on near-tie sets, and add telemetry to track rerank inversion rate per workspace.

Customer communication: Findly notified 2026-03-11 about workaround; follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-13 to coordinate re-testing and safe re-enable of optimized path.
